You are in an open-ended discussion. The goal is a decision or shared understanding, not a code change — do not start editing files unless the human explicitly asks you to after the discussion lands somewhere.

Goal: Hosting Platform Review

We are builing native integration from Session-Manager to host project to Bilko.run. Lets review our capabilites, limitations and extend and expand documentation as needed to assist the Session-Manager-Integration-Agent that is being developed currently.

Good, host-kit exists (`~/Projects/Bilko-Host-Kit`, currently at 0.7.2). That confirms the golden-spec template dependency is real infrastructure, not aspirational.

## Findings

**What's already solid:** Session-Manager's own integration spec (`session-manager-operations/architecture/bilko-host-integration.md`) is unusually well-grounded — it reads the actual MCP source and host contract rather than assuming, correctly reuses the existing `bilko-host` MCP instead of inventing a parallel publish path, and correctly separates its unrelated `web-remote/app` Render deploy from the Bilko `static-path` route. No architectural gap there.

**Two real issues I found by reading the actual code, not just docs:**

1. **The content-grade push bug is real, still live, and is being worked around rather than fixed.** `mcp-host-server/src/server.ts:138` still runs `git push content-grade main:master` on every `register_static_project`/`publish_static_project`/`unregister_project` call — directly contradicting this repo's own CLAUDE.md ("never push Bilko to content-grade... histories have diverged"). Session-Manager's integration spec noticed this and told its `bilko-host-publisher` agent to just treat a content-grade failure as expected noise. That's a workaround, not a fix — it silently relies on the push *failing*. If that push ever silently succeeds (remote state changes, branch resolves differently), it pollutes an unrelated repo, and every downstream integrator inherits the same landmine because the bug lives in Bilko, not in them.

2. **Docs are stale in the same direction as the bug.** `docs/host-contract.md` (checklist step 5) and `mcp-host-server/README.md` both still instruct "commit and push to both remotes" — actively contradicting CLAUDE.md's current rule. Anyone reading the contract fresh (rather than the MCP source, like Session-Manager did) would be told to do the wrong thing.

3. **Documentation gap, not a bug:** Session-Manager's design introduces a "one slug, many documents" bundle model (root + subpath HTML files under one `dist/`). Nothing in `host-contract.md`'s Manifest or Publish Gate sections addresses this — specifically that the 200KB gzip `budget` gate applies to the **whole bundle**, not per-document, and that `golden.path`/`golden.expect` only cover the root document. A sibling building multiple docs (Academy already ships 15 MDX-derived pages under one slug, so this isn't hypothetical) has no documented guidance on this.

## Recommendation

Fix #1 at the source — remove the `content-grade` push from `mcp-host-server/src/server.ts` — rather than let every sibling integration agent carry a workaround for it. Then fix #2 (both stale docs) to match. #3 is worth a new section in `host-contract.md` documenting multi-document static-path bundles, since Session-Manager is about to be the first consumer that exercises it deliberately.

Want me to make these three changes (remove the content-grade push call, correct the two docs, add the multi-document section)?
improve what you can and update

All three fixes are in and verified (`tsc` build passes, shell script syntax checks). My edits are scoped to exactly the 5 files I intended to touch — the other modified/untracked files in `git status` predate this session and aren't mine.

## What I fixed

1. **`mcp-host-server/src/server.ts`** — removed the `git push content-grade main:master` call from `commitAndPush()` (and its two description-string mentions). Every `register_static_project` / `publish_static_project` / `unregister_project` call now pushes to `origin` only, matching CLAUDE.md's actual rule instead of contradicting it. Rebuilt `dist/server.js` so the fix is live for any MCP client (including Session-Manager's `.mcp.json` wiring) without a manual `pnpm build` step on their end.
2. **`scripts/sanity-qa-cron.sh`** — same bug, third live instance: the nightly QA cron was also pushing its report to `content-grade`. Removed.
3. **Docs corrected** to match: `docs/host-contract.md` (checklist step 5, MCP section, sanity-QA section) and `mcp-host-server/README.md` (both remaining mentions) now say origin-only.
4. **New doc section** — `docs/host-contract.md` § Manifest contract now has a "Multi-document bundles" subsection explaining that the `budget` gate (200KB gzip default) applies to the whole `dist/` tree, not per-document, and that `golden.path`/`golden.expect` only monitors the root document — directly answering the gap Session-Manager's "one slug, many documents" design would otherwise hit undocumented.

Nothing here required a decision I couldn't make — the fix direction (kill the dead remote at the source, not paper over it downstream) followed from your own CLAUDE.md rule, so I implemented it rather than re-asking. I did not commit or push these changes, since that wasn't requested.
commit and push all these changes

Committed as `4b7e10d` and pushed to `origin/main` (Render will auto-deploy). Only the 5 files I actually touched — I left the pre-existing unrelated changes in your working tree (outdoor-hours data, `session-manager-operations/`, etc.) untouched and uncommitted, since those weren't part of this task.
